==English==
{{wp}}

===Etymology===
From {{bor|en|fr|épisode}}, from {{der|en|la-new|*epīsodium}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἐπεισόδιον||a parenthetic addition, episode}}, neuter of {{m|grc|ἐπεισόδιος||following upon the entrance, coming in besides, adventitious}}, from {{m|grc|ἐπί||on}} + {{m|grc|εἰς||into}} + {{m|grc|ὁδός||way}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛp.ɪ.səʊd/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɛp.ə.soʊd/|a=GA}}
** {{audio|en|en-us-episode.ogg|a=GA}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈep.ɪ.səʉd/|a=AU}}
* {{hyphenation|en|epi|sode}}
* {{rhymes|en|əʊd|s=3}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# A [[discrete]] but [[connected]] [[event]], [[situation]], or [[period]] within a [[broad]]er [[sequence]], [[narrative]], or [[life]] [[course]].
#: {{syn|en|event|proceeding|Thesaurus:occurrence}}
#: {{ux|en|It was a most embarrassing '''episode''' in my life.}}
# {{lb|en|film|radio|television}} A [[bounded]] [[narrative]] unit within a [[television series]], constituting a single installment that is [[structurally]] [[discrete]] yet [[interrelated]] with the series as a whole.
#: {{hypo|en|bottle episode}}
#: {{ux|en|I can't wait till next week’s '''episode'''.}}
